name: PubMed / NCBI E-utilities Vocabulary
description: Key terms, acronyms, and concepts used in the PubMed and NCBI E-utilities API ecosystem.

terms.definition: PubMed Identifier. A unique integer assigned to each article in the PubMed database. Used to retrieve specific records via EFetch and ESummary.
PubMed Central Identifier. A unique identifier (format: PMC followed by digits) for articles archived in PubMed Central (PMC).
Digital Object Identifier. A persistent identifier assigned to journal articles for stable linking across publishers.
Medical Subject Headings. The controlled vocabulary thesaurus maintained by the National Library of Medicine (NLM) for indexing and searching biomedical literature in PubMed.

National Center for Biotechnology Information. A branch of the National Library of Medicine (NLM) that provides access to biomedical databases including PubMed, GenBank, and 38 other Entrez databases.
National Library of Medicine. The world's largest biomedical library, which maintains PubMed and MeSH.
The integrated, text-based search and retrieval system used at NCBI for all major databases including PubMed, Protein, Nucleotide, Gene, Structure, and more.

Entrez Programming Utilities. A set of nine server-side programs that provide API access to all Entrez databases. Includes ESearch, EFetch, ESummary, ELink, EPost, EInfo, ESpell, EGQuery, and ECitMatch.
E-utility for searching Entrez databases. Returns a list of UIDs matching a text query. Results can be cached on the History server.
E-utility for retrieving full records from Entrez databases. Supports multiple return types (abstract, medline, FASTA, GenBank) and modes (xml, text, asn.1).
E-utility for retrieving document summaries (DocSums) for specified UIDs. Returns abbreviated metadata in XML or JSON format.
E-utility for finding records linked to a set of input UIDs, either within the same database or across different Entrez databases. Also provides LinkOut URLs to external resources.
E-utility for uploading a list of UIDs to the Entrez History server for use in subsequent calls. Returns a WebEnv and query_key.
E-utility for retrieving information about Entrez databases including field names, link names, and statistics.
E-utility for retrieving spelling suggestions for search terms within an Entrez database.
E-utility for performing a global query across all Entrez databases and returning hit counts per database.
E-utility for converting citation strings (journal, year, volume, page, author) to PubMed IDs.
Web Environment string. A server-side session token returned by ESearch (with usehistory=y), EPost, and ELink to store sets of UIDs on the Entrez History server for reuse across multiple calls.
An integer assigned to each set of UIDs stored on the Entrez History server within a WebEnv session.
Unique Identifier. An integer identifier assigned to each record in an Entrez database (e.g., PMID for PubMed).
Retrieval mode parameter. Controls the output format of E-utility responses. Common values: xml, json, text, asn.1.
Retrieval type parameter. Controls the type of record returned by EFetch. Values vary by database. For PubMed: abstract, medline, uilist, docsum.
Maximum number of records to retrieve in a single E-utility call. Default is 20; maximum is 100,000 for ESearch and 10,000 for EFetch/ESummary.
Sequential index of the first record to retrieve in a paginated E-utility response.
PubMed Central. NCBI's free full-text archive of biomedical and life sciences journal literature. Provides OA articles, OAI-PMH harvesting, BioC API, and ID conversion services.
Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting. A standard for metadata interoperability used by PMC to enable bulk harvesting of article metadata.
A simple XML/JSON format for biological data and NLP interchange. Used by the PMC BioC API to provide structured full-text content for text mining applications.
Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online. The primary component of PubMed, providing access to over 25 million references from more than 5,200 journals. Records include MeSH terms.
A brief summary of a scientific article, typically including purpose, methods, results, and conclusions. Widely available in PubMed for indexed articles.
Optional NCBI API key that increases the request rate limit from 3 requests/second to 10 requests/second. Obtained by registering at NCBI.
NCBI program that links PubMed records to relevant external resources including full-text articles, sequences, clinical resources, and more via ELink.
Document Summary. An abbreviated record returned by ESummary containing key metadata fields for each UID.
